taxonomic_note: Reviewed accepted Matelea parvifolia species concept (research-drafts/matelea-parvifolia/draft.json); do not conflate with Central Texas Matelea reticulata or M. edwardsensis.
look_here_first: Look at leaf SIZE and flower SHAPE together: a wiry desert twiner with very small 0.5–2 cm leaves and tiny bell-shaped flowers with short triangular (2–3 mm) corolla lobes. Confirm the five-ridged cup-shaped corona at magnification.

best_field_traits: Slender, drought-deciduous, suffrutescent twining plant; shoots roughly 10–150 cm
Small ovate to lanceolate or deltate leaves, approximately 0.5–2 cm long
Very small campanulate brown/maroon-to-green flowers, not strongly net-reticulate
Short deltate corolla lobes approximately 2–3 mm long
Cup-shaped corona with five ridges; inspect style apex at close range
Narrow follicle about 5–9 cm long, nearly smooth to sparsely tuberculate
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Flower and corona characters plus leaf dimensions are more reliable than flower color alone. Photograph leaf and flower beside a ruler.

comparisons.key_distinctions: M. sagittifolia has longer oblong-spatulate corolla lobes and a white lobed style apex; M. parvifolia has minute triangular lobes and a green-to-maroon pentagonal style apex. Chthamalia biflora is a low, densely hairy herb with larger leaves and paired dark flowers, not a wiry tiny-leaved desert twiner. M. reticulata has larger, broad, strongly netted flowers with silvery center; M. edwardsensis has larger pale green bell-shaped flowers with longitudinal markings and distinct corona segments.
